cards.explanation: The answer is in God's hands. The Teacher says "…the righteous and the wise, as well as their deeds, are in God’s hands." That covers the people and their deeds. I think that's a comfort, friends, because nobody has to hold it all together alone. (Ecclesiastes 9:1)

The answer is False. The Teacher says "Man does not know what lies ahead, whether love or hate." Nobody gets a crystal ball, not the righteous and not the wise. I can't even call a batch before it comes out, and I've got a window on my oven. (Ecclesiastes 9:1)

The answer is that they share a common fate. The Teacher says "There is a common fate for the righteous and the wicked, for the good and the bad…" Then he keeps stacking pairs: clean and unclean, the one who sacrifices and the one who does not. It's a hard list, friends, and he doesn't sugarcoat a single pair. (Ecclesiastes 9:2)

The answer is True. The Teacher says "…the hearts of men are full of evil and madness while they are alive…" (Ecclesiastes 9:3). That's a hard line, and he doesn't dress it up. The very next verse says "There is hope, however, for anyone who is among the living…" (Ecclesiastes 9:4).

The answer is True. The Teacher says "…even a live dog is better than a dead lion." The lion is the famous fierce one, and the dog is just a dog. Still, the one that's breathing wins. He's backing up the hope he just gave to anyone among the living. (Ecclesiastes 9:4)

The answer is that the living know they will die. The Teacher says "For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing." It's an odd thing to call an advantage, friends, but he sets it right beside the hope of the living. I think knowing it means the living still have time to use. (Ecclesiastes 9:5)

The reason he gives is that the memory of them is forgotten. The Teacher says "They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten." It's a heavy line, and he states it plainly. He doesn't say any more about it than that. (Ecclesiastes 9:5)

The answer is True. The Teacher says "Their love, their hate, and their envy have already vanished, and they will never again have a share in all that is done under the sun." It's a short list and a blunt one. I think he's showing how different things are for the living. (Ecclesiastes 9:6)

His reason is that God has already approved your works. The Teacher says to eat your bread with joy and drink your wine with a cheerful heart, "…for God has already approved your works." Notice the order, friends: the approval comes first, and the enjoying follows. Eating with joy is about the easiest job in my bakery, and I've had a lot of practice. (Ecclesiastes 9:7)

The answer is your beloved wife. The Teacher says "Enjoy life with your beloved wife…" He means it for all your fleeting days. Notice the word is enjoy life, friends, not just get through it. (Ecclesiastes 9:9)

The answer is False. The Teacher says "…the fleeting life that God has given you under the sun…" and "…all your fleeting days." He calls it fleeting, not long and lasting. And the verse opens with the words "Enjoy life…" (Ecclesiastes 9:9)

The answer is with all your might. The Teacher says "Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might…" That means full effort, no coasting. When I stamp a cookie, my mustache and I go in so hard the flour files a complaint. (Ecclesiastes 9:10)

His reason is that in Sheol there is no work. He says to work with all your might "…for in Sheol, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom." Sheol is where the dead go. I think it tells us, friends, the time for work is the time we have right now. (Ecclesiastes 9:10)

The answer is True. The Teacher says "The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong…" The fastest runner doesn't always take the prize, and the strongest fighter doesn't always win. He's about to say the same thing about bread, wealth and favor. (Ecclesiastes 9:11)

The reason is that time and chance happen to all. The Teacher says "For time and chance happen to all." You can plan the whole batch and still have the power flicker. Swift or slow, strong or not, it reaches everybody. (Ecclesiastes 9:11)

The answer is fish caught in a cruel net. The Teacher says men are ensnared "Like fish caught in a cruel net or birds trapped in a snare…" Two pictures of being caught, friends. He says the evil time "…suddenly falls upon them." (Ecclesiastes 9:12)
